description: Stable unique identifier for the model; do not change once assigned.
Common name or acronym used for the model.
Formal or expanded model name.
Named individual developer(s), when documented.
Organization primarily responsible for model development.
Approximate year the model/system was first developed.
Province(s), territory/territories, or other jurisdictional scope associated with the model.
Broad model class.
More specific structural description, such as empirical, mechanistic, semi-empirical, distance-independent, or distance-dependent.
Forest or stand types for which the model was developed or documented.
Species or species groups covered by the model. Use standard species codes where possible; multiple values separated by ';'.
Geographic area represented by the calibration/development data; detailed polygons belong in the coverage dataset.
Geographic area represented by independent validation/testing, when documented.
Region explicitly identified by the developer for intended application.
Important model inputs. Multiple values separated by ';'.
Important model outputs. Multiple values separated by ';'.
Whether mortality is represented.
Whether regeneration is represented or projected.
Whether commercial thinning can be represented; distinguish capability from validated thinning response in notes or a later management table.
Whether precommercial thinning can be represented.
Whether fertilization scenarios/response can be represented.
Whether pruning scenarios/response can be represented.
Major disturbances represented or supported, such as fire, insects, wind, or harvest; multiple values separated by ';'.
Whether climate variables or climate-driven responses are explicitly represented.
Programming language(s) or implementation technology used by the native model.
How users interact with the model, such as R package, executable, GUI, spreadsheet, web app, or API.
Whether source code is publicly available.
Public URL to source code or repository, when available.
Whether model documentation/manual is publicly available.
Public URL to the principal model manual/documentation.
Primary publication or technical reference supporting the model.
Language(s) of the principal model documentation.
Current lifecycle/status of the model in the registry.
Date on which the registry record was last checked against its sources.
How completely the record has been verified.
Additional qualifications, limitations, ambiguities, or interpretation notes.
